A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AudioCOCO and human-versus-AI sound localization study. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Revised protocols and internal inconsistencies require caution when interpreting performance differences.

before.justification: v1 reports original human psychophysics, model evaluations, and IS3 fine-tuning experiments, including results in Section 3, Table 1, and Table S1.

after.justification: v2 reports original human and EchoPin experiments, including component comparisons, an ear-rotation intervention, metric sensitivity analyses, and additional benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 fine-tunes IS3 with a convolutional adapter for stereo input. v2 introduces EchoPin, adding KEMAR HRTF filtering and ERB-based cochleagrams while retaining the IS3 encoders and stereo-fusion approach. These substantially change auditory processing; EchoPin is not merely a renamed IS3-FT.

E1.justification: The six AudioCOCO conditions and twelve object categories remain. Section S5 and Table S3 add fine-tuning and evaluation on VGG-SS and Flickr-SoundNet, extending benchmark coverage within the same SSL task. AudioCOCO sample-count and split revisions change the protocol rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: The eight external model baselines remain in the comprehensive appendix comparison. Table 1b revises the internal comparisons to EchoPin-M, EchoPin-S, and full EchoPin, and no longer reports stereo-IS3 results. Figure S10 also adds CAVP to the qualitative comparisons previously focused on IS3.

E3.justification: AudioCOCO changes from 1,003,747 reported pairs to 9,360 training and 18,864 test pairs. Human sampling changes from 15 participants/4,050 trials to 14/2,100. A-Acc changes from segmentation-mask membership to bounding-box membership, all model evaluations receive HRTF-filtered audio, and fine-tuning changes from SGD to Adam with revised hyperparameters. Appendix S1 retains conflicting source-split wording.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's mono/stereo comparisons and failure cases, v2 adds cochleagram component comparisons and an interaural-axis rotation experiment testing the origin of localization asymmetry. New chance-normalized accuracy and 0/10/25-pixel tolerance analyses examine evaluation robustness. Additional qualitative comparisons analyze CAVP's failures.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three model evaluation runs with different random seeds in Section S3 and SEM error bars in Figure 4's caption. Neither introduces a new confidence-interval, significance-testing, or repeated-run reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised: congruent A-Acc for IS3-FT-Stereo is 19.3/29.1/52.2% in v1, versus 11.2/50.9/76.0% for EchoPin in v2. Figure 7 reverses the displayed silence-versus-noise trend. v2 adds benchmark results and reports EchoPin exceeding humans for size-3 multi-instance localization, 47.1% versus 38.6%. Changed models, data, and scoring prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section S5 introduces the formal definition Gain(X) = 100 × (Acc_X − Acc_rand)/Acc_rand and reasoning about correcting object-area effects. v1 has no corresponding definition. This is a limited mathematical addition without new theorems or proofs; Table S1's reported percentages are inconsistent with the formula's factor of 100.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion shift the method contribution from fine-tuning an existing model on better stereo data to introducing EchoPin with biologically motivated HRTF and cochlear processing. The claimed explanation for human-like localization expands accordingly. The overarching modality-bias and human-versus-AI claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes localization asymmetry to cochlear processing and stereo geometry, presenting ear rotation as confirmation of its structural origin. It reverses the interpretation of auditory noise from strengthening visual bias to reducing visual reliance, and adds interpretations of metric robustness. Some new interpretations conflict with tables: EchoPin's size-2 audio-only accuracy is higher with noise than gray backgrounds, contrary to the prose.

D1.justification: v2 adds HRTF-source and cochleagram implementation details, including sampling rate, filter count, tensor dimensions, preprocessing storage, ten training epochs, and approximately sixteen hours per fine-tuning session. Hardware and optimization details are revised. The promise to release resources becomes an availability statement with a repository link; its external contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the auditory-neuroscience positioning through HRTF, KEMAR, cochlear-processing, and temporal-coding literature, alongside additional spatial-audio references. These support a newly foregrounded neuroscience-inspired model contribution. The existing SSL literature and the earlier Francl–McDermott localization reference largely remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, results interpretations, and discussion are rewritten around EchoPin. The former methods-and-metrics subsection becomes separate EchoPin and baseline/evaluation subsections, and the appendix gains Section S5. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond terminology changes or added results alone.

P2.justification: A new EchoPin diagram occupies Figure 3, while the earlier baseline overview is adapted and moved to Figure S7. Figure 6 adds the rotated-ear variant, Table 1 changes structure, and qualitative heatmaps are revised. The appendix adds training-distribution figures, CAVP visualizations, and three quantitative tables; the former comprehensive Table S1 becomes Table S4.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly observational explanation of localization asymmetry, v2 provides useful component and ear-rotation tests, additional benchmark validation, metric sensitivity checks, and fuller implementation documentation. These improve evidential support and reproducibility. The overall gain is limited by reporting problems, including Table S1's percentage-scaling error, conflicting mask-versus-box descriptions, and retained blanket human-superiority claims despite contrary results in Table 1a.
